evidence.quote: The trees flower from September to May (southern hemisphere) and the rather special fruit is produced from December to July.

harvestMonths.notes: PZA does not break this down by province; the species is described there as growing across most of the country, so this is treated as a general/national figure. It is a very long flowering/fruiting window (8 months) rather than a sharp harvest season.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Set to null in editor review: 21.85 kg is SEED weight for oil extraction from wild trees (a conference abstract), and the app would show it as a tree's fruit crop. Withdrawn value: [21.85, 21.85].

evidence.quote: In this study it was found that the trees are andromonoecious, starting with male flowers and switching to the production of female flowers.
evidence.doc: ASHS 2011 Annual Conference abstract - DuToit, Cloete & Robbertse, University of Pretoria

pollination.notes: Species is reported as andromonoecious (male and hermaphrodite flowers on the same plant, sequentially). This does not map cleanly onto the schema's pollination categories, and no source made an explicit self-fertile/needs-cross-pollinator statement, so left null rather than forcing a category.

gaps: yearsToFirstCrop / yearsToFullBearing: searched SANBI PlantZAfrica and the ASHS 2011 abstract - neither gives an age to first fruiting or full bearing; PZA only notes germination takes six to ten weeks and that 'saplings are slow-growing especially when young'.
chillUnits: no source discusses a chilling requirement for this species (it is described as both cold- and heat-tolerant on PZA, but that is not a chill-unit figure).

A ScienceDirect paper on Pappea capensis gender expression (S. Afr. J. Bot., pii S0254629910002590) was found via search but the article page returned 403 Forbidden (paywalled) - could not be fetched to check for additional yield/pollination detail.
